brief.headline: HBM4E Race Accelerates as SK Hynix Pulls Sample Timeline Forward; Memory ASP Surge Continues
brief.summary: <cite index="36-8,36-9">SK Hynix is prepared to provide HBM4E samples to major customers as early as this month, ahead of its prior 2H timeline.</cite> <cite index="36-2">Samsung delivered first 12-layer 48GB HBM4E samples on May 29.</cite> <cite index="5-1">Jensen Huang confirmed all three memory makers passed HBM4 qualification and are moving into mass production.</cite> <cite index="12-2,12-8">DRAM contract prices are rising 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 following a 90-95% QoQ surge in Q1, while NAND Flash is jumping 70-75% QoQ.</cite> <cite index="21-2,21-6">Hyperscalers committed $660-690 billion in 2026 capex, nearly doubling 2025 levels, with ~75% directed at AI compute.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="7-6">UBS predicts SK Hynix will achieve approximately 70% market share in HBM4 for NVIDIA's Rubin platform in 2026.</cite> <cite index="40-5,40-6">SK Hynix's HBM market share reportedly dipped from ~69% to 58% YoY as Samsung and Micron ramp, with analysts warning Samsung's HBM4 catch-up could trigger a valuation re-rating.</cite> <cite index="38-5">Samsung holds 35% HBM market share in Q3 2025 versus SK Hynix's 53%.</cite> Short-term edge to SK Hynix on execution velocity and customer lock, but Samsung's HBM4E timing advantage (May 29 first samples) and AMD MI450 design win narrow the delta. Watch for NVIDIA allocation announcements and 2H HBM4E qualification outcomes. Relative multiple compression risk tilts toward Samsung if it fails to convert timing into volume share.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="9-2,9-3">Conventional DRAM prices increased 55-60% QoQ in Q1 2026 and NAND 33-38% QoQ, driven by widening supply-demand gap as CSPs secure capacity and suppliers maintain disciplined output.</cite> <cite index="12-9,12-10">DRAM suppliers reallocating capacity toward AI-related applications, NAND directed toward enterprise SSDs, with meaningful capacity expansion not expected until late 2027 at earliest.</cite> <cite index="10-5,10-6">Samsung and SK Hynix (70% of global DRAM) signaled no aggressive capacity expansion, prioritizing profitability over volume.</cite> <cite index="10-7">Analysts projected memory price rally extending past 2028.</cite> Bit supply constrained by HBM conversion cannibalizing legacy DRAM/NAND wafer starts. Pricing power intact through 2027.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-1">All three memory makers passed HBM4 qualification tests and are now moving into mass production.</cite> <cite index="5-8,5-10">SK Hynix placed 44.2 billion won order with Hanmi Semiconductor for TC bonders for HBM4 production, with equipment expected at Cheongju back-end facility.</cite> <cite index="3-1">HBM3E will account for ~two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026, with HBM4 gradually gaining traction.</cite> <cite index="1-2,1-6">Samsung and SK Hynix expected to prioritize HBM4 ramp, keeping HBM3E supply tight and lagging demand.</cite> <cite index="36-3">TrendForce predicts HBM4E will account for 40% of overall HBM demand by 2027.</cite> <cite index="1-5">H200 export approval to China (each H200 incorporates six stacks of HBM3E) exceeded demand expectations.</cite> <cite index="40-7,40-8">HBM4 involves projected 50% increase in cost per bit, with companies expecting 40% higher prices, but $20.5 billion capex and rising supplier prices could pressure margins if ASP growth slows.</cite> Key risk: Samsung/SK simultaneous HBM4E ramp could compress premiums faster than expected in 2H.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix accelerates HBM4E sample delivery to June vs. prior 2H guidance
news_pulse.implication: Competitive pressure from Samsung's May 29 HBM4E sample delivery forcing SK Hynix to pull forward timeline. Shares +7% on news. Increases probability of 4Q26 HBM4E revenue contribution.

news_pulse.headline: Jensen Huang confirms all three memory makers passed HBM4 qualification, moving to mass production
news_pulse.implication: De-risks Samsung HBM4 qualification concerns. Micron now qualified alongside Samsung/SK Hynix, intensifying 2H allocation battle. Nvidia Rubin platform supply secured across three vendors.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, NAND +70-75% QoQ per TrendForce
news_pulse.implication: NAND now outpacing DRAM ASP growth for first time this cycle. Enterprise SSD-driven NAND tightness structural through 2027. Legacy DRAM/NAND buyers facing sticker shock; supports continued margin expansion for Samsung/SK Hynix conventional memory segments.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to $660-690 billion, up 81% YoY, 75% AI-directed
news_pulse.implication: HBM/CoWoS/enterprise SSD demand visibility extends into 2027.供給 constraint narrative intact. Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, Microsoft $120B+, Oracle $50B aggregate spend locked.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity targeting 115-140k wafers/month by end-2026, 170k by 2027
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS bottleneck easing but still tight. Nvidia secured 60% of 2026 capacity. HBM production constrained by packaging availability through 1H27. Samsung/SK Hynix back-end capex justification reinforced.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix consider first packaging plants in Honam region
news_pulse.implication: Geographic diversification signaling confidence in multi-year HBM capex cycle. Samsung Electro-Mechanics reviewing additional FC-BGA capacity at Sejong for AI server substrates. Supply chain localization reduces geopolitical risk but adds 2027+ capacity, not near-term relief.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix struck 900k DRAM wafers/month supply deal with OpenAI for Stargate
news_pulse.implication: Stargate LOI signed October 2025. Samsung P5 Pyeongtaek operational 2028, SK Hynix M15X mid-2027. Near-term supply already allocated; incremental capacity targets hyperscaler LTAs. Validates multi-year capex upcycle for both names.

news_pulse.headline: Leverage Shares lists 3x leveraged Samsung/SK Hynix ETPs on LSE June 12
news_pulse.implication: Retail/institutional access via London expands global liquidity. 3x long-only products (SMG3, HNX3) implemented via KRX futures. Potential volatility amplifier and gamma feedback loop on strong momentum days.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="39-2,39-3,39-7,39-10">3x leveraged ETPs for Samsung (SMG3) and SK Hynix (HNX3) launched on LSE June 12, implemented through Samsung/SK Hynix futures on KRX, expected to enhance global investor access and expand derivatives market utilization.</cite> <cite index="35-2,35-14">Samsung rose 6.05% and SK Hynix 5.3% in premarket trading June 15 on U.S.-Iran war-ending deal.</cite> <cite index="36-1,36-7">SK Hynix shares +7% (2.3M KRW) on HBM4E sample news, Samsung +5.35%, driving KOSPI up >5%.</cite> Options OI likely building into July expiry on both names. Watch for gamma squeeze if momentum continues; 3x ETP structure could amplify intraday swings. Volatility surface likely steepening on upside strikes given HBM4E timeline pull-forward and qualification de-risking.

Any NVIDIA commentary on HBM4/HBM4E allocation splits between Samsung/SK Hynix/Micron following Huang's qualification confirmation

3x leveraged ETP (SMG3/HNX3) trading volumes and premium/discount to NAV on LSE debut; potential flow-back pressure on KRX futures
